cover_title:
Pho, cocktails,
and karaoke
on Route 1 North.
Come out tonight.
cover_thesis: Street-born Vietnamese energy — warm, moody, and built for a night out.
s01_feel: The brand should feel like: a warm, low-lit Vietnamese bar where the night starts at a barstool and ends with karaoke — energetic but never loud, moody but never cold. Not like: a family noodle shop with checkered tablecloths, stock photography, and "authentic Vietnamese cuisine" on repeat.
s02_rationale: Editorial / Human at 70% anchors the brand in real atmosphere — documentary photography, warm copy that invites you out tonight rather than advertising at you. The 30% Cutting-edge / Innovative layer prevents the brand from reading as a generic neighborhood spot; it shows up in sharp typographic contrast, the neon logo mark, and the Spicy Pho Ti-Ni cocktail identity. The balance keeps Quán Phở feeling fresh and night-out ready without drifting into trend-chasing.
s02_prevents:
• Heavy editorial direction alone → the 30% innovative edge keeps hierarchy sharp and CTAs legible
  • Generic innovation styling alone → the 70% human anchor keeps warmth and approachability intact
  • Overly polished lifestyle photography → the editorial direction keeps subjects real and specific to this location
  • Marketing jargon or superlatives → the human direction grounds all copy in present-tense specifics
s03_h2: Dark warm palette with a gold anchor
s03_intro: Neutrals run from near-black base (#181008) through warm brown surface (#241810) and hold 65% of every page — the darkness is the atmosphere, not a layer on top. Gold #F2B928 is the sole interactive anchor across all CTAs, hover states, and display type; crimson #C23528 appears in one section only, the bar promo strip.
s03_ratio_note:
The 65/20/10 ratio keeps the visual weight on atmosphere. Gold leads every call to action; crimson lands exactly once — on the bar promo strip — so it never loses its punch.

65% Neutrals20% Gold anchor10% Crimson accent
s03_never:
• White or light backgrounds on any full-page section — the darkness is the brand atmosphere
  • Crimson #C23528 as a primary interactive or navigation color — reserved for the bar promo strip only
  • Neon green #52E074 on any element outside the logo mark
  • Blue, purple, or cool-toned accent colors not in the locked palette
  • Semi-transparent gold that washes out on dark — use full-opacity #F2B928 for interactive elements
s04_intro: Be Vietnam Pro handles approximately 90% of the interface — body copy, navigation, labels, and CTA buttons — in Regular for reading and Bold for headings and interactive elements. Cormorant Garamond Italic is reserved for the 10% of high-impact display moments: the hero tagline and section separators. No third typeface is introduced; this pairing is complete and locked.

s07_h2: Build trust with what's already real
s07_intro: Quán Phở carries medium trust burden: less than six months of reviews, early Yelp feedback that's polarized, and a bar and karaoke offering not yet visible on the current site. The strategy is to lead with what's confirmed — the Google 5-star reviews, the Long's Noodle House lineage, the physical bar — and let the experience convert the skeptic.
s07_phases:
Phase 1 — now

Launch with confirmed proof

  • Show 3 confirmed 5-star Google reviews in the homepage proof band
  • Display Yelp 4.0★ (9 reviews) in the credential bar
  • Feature "formerly Long's Noodle House — same family, same address" as hero trust copy
Phase 2 — as the brand grows

Stack social and community proof

  • Add a Google Business Profile review widget as volume grows past 25 reviews
  • Pull a featured 5-star quote for the Cormorant Garamond large-scale quote section
  • Collect photo testimonials from karaoke nights and bar events for the social band
s07_no_fabricate:
• Do not display a star rating unless the exact confirmed number is used — Yelp 4.0★ and Google 5-star only
  • Do not write "hundreds of happy guests" or similar estimates without confirmed data
  • Do not reference delivery or a party booking process until the client confirms the details
  • Do not claim "best pho in Boston" or any superlative without a cited source
  • Do not invent a founder story — the Long's Noodle House lineage is confirmed; biography details are not
s08_h2: Photography-first: moody interiors, close-up food, bar energy
s08_photo_table: Photography directionEnvironment-led + Product-led + People-ledSubject priorityPlace (bar, interior atmosphere) first; Product (food close-ups) second; People (group bar energy) thirdMoodWarm, Intimate, Energetic — evening atmosphereLightingMoody — existing dark high-quality interior shots are the reference standard; warm overhead pendants, not studio whiteCompositionClose-up for food; medium-wide for interior/bar; candid-to-documentary for people at the barIllustration / icon directionNone — photo-only; full photo library confirmed
s08_never:
• Stock photography of any kind — only images from the confirmed Quán Phở photo library
  • Bright, studio-lit, white-background food photography
  • Posed or solo headshot photography — bar energy requires candid group shots
  • Flat-lay or overhead aerial food compositions
  • Illustrations, icons, or graphic overlays placed on photographs
  • Neon color filters or Instagram-style grading that departs from the warm dark palette
  • Photography styled for a daytime café or family-friendly setting
s09_motion_table: LevelRestrainedRoleReveal + HoverScroll behaviorFade-up — sections fade in from 12px below, 300ms ease; not staggered; not dramaticButton hoverGold #F2B928 dims to #E0A820, 150ms ease transition; no scale transform, no glowReduced motionRequired — all scroll animations must respect prefers-reduced-motion
s09_no_animate:
• Parallax effects on the hero image or any full-bleed photography section
  • Staggered or sequenced scroll animations — all sections fade in uniformly at 300ms
  • Scale transforms on button hover — gold color shift only, no grow or shrink
  • Animated background gradients, color cycling, or shimmer effects
  • Looping video backgrounds or auto-play media of any kind
  • Any animation that does not include a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce override

s13_preserve:
• Cormorant Garamond Italic in warm gold #F2B928 for the hero tagline and any display-scale section separator — do not substitute another serif
  • Gold #F2B928 CTA button placed above the fold on every major conversion section
  • Bar promo strip in crimson #C23528 — the only full-section red moment; never extend crimson to other sections
  • Neon green #52E074 restricted to the logo mark only — apply nowhere else
  • Dual CTAs in hero above the fold: Order Now (gold filled) and Book a Party (gold outline)
  • Dark near-black backgrounds on all page sections — no white or light-mode sections
  • "Formerly Long's Noodle House — same family, same address" preserved as hero trust copy until superseded by higher review volume
s13_a11y:
• All text on dark backgrounds must meet WCAG AA contrast — gold #F2B928 on #181008 passes at ~8.1:1; cream #F0E8D0 on #181008 passes at ~13:1
  • All scroll fade-up animations must include @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { animation: none; transition: none; }
  • CTA buttons must carry descriptive labels — "Order Now" and "Book a Party", never generic "Click here" or "Learn more"
  • All photography must include descriptive alt text: food subject, composition, and mood — not filename or empty alt
  • Proof chips and credential bar must not be the sole trust signal — pair with semantic heading structure and body copy
  • Future party booking form inputs must use associated <label> elements, not placeholder text alone
  • Interactive color changes (button hover from #F2B928 to #E0A820) must be accompanied by a visible focus indicator for keyboard users
s13_no_improvise:
• Do not introduce a third typeface — Be Vietnam Pro + Cormorant Garamond is the complete locked system
  • Do not apply neon green #52E074 to any element outside the logo mark under any circumstance
  • Do not add delivery CTA copy until the client confirms a delivery platform and service zone
  • Do not design or activate the party booking flow until capacity and deposit process are confirmed with the client
  • Do not add a language switcher without confirmed bilingual content needs from the client
